transcript:
Meeting header - 2026-11-10 16:00 PT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (MeridianPay CTO), Aisha Khan (MeridianPay SRE), Ben Thomson (MeridianPay Product)

Summary: Weekly POC check-in for latency tuning. Focus: TTFT, streaming behavior, sequence length distribution, kernel choices and quantization tradeoffs.

Topics covered: TTFT baseline and target, streaming vs full-response tradeoffs, kernel selection and quantization, KV/prefix cache hit rates, test plan for 1-hour streaming run.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have 45 minutes, quick agenda — benchmark recap, tuning items, decide on next short tests.
00:08 Carlos: yep thanks, we've got limited time too so, um, biggest pain is first token sometimes spikes to 350-400ms which breaks our checkout flow.
00:17 Priya: okay, that's higher than ideal, our hosted numbers on the model variant we gave you showed about 120-150ms median and 220ms 95th, so curious what your load pattern looks like.
00:25 Carlos: we're seeing a bimodal pattern — quick small prompts from fraud checks, and then longer 700-1,200 token prompts for full assistant flows. The TTFT spikes are correlated with the long ones but also on cold starts.
00:42 Ben: we also noticed when streaming is enabled the UI shows a big blank for the first 300ms then chunked tokens, which feels slow even if throughput after that is fine.
00:55 Priya: couple things to call out — TTFT is influenced by scheduling, kernel selection for the first decode step, and whether the KV cache is warm. For streaming specifically, the initial decode path sometimes has extra overhead if we need to JIT a different kernel for long context.
01:12 Jordan: right, so the knobs we can tweak right now: pin model to a lower-latency kernel variant, force early-init of kernels during request start up, warm prefix/KV cache on session start, or change streaming chunk sizes. Also quantization mode affects first token latency slightly.
01:33 Aisha: when you say pin to kernel variant, do you mean a smaller attention kernel or a different GEMM backend? We have strict compliance threads so we can't change inference RAM footprint much.
01:45 Priya: good Q — we mean choosing between the fused mha attention kernel vs the generic matmul path. Fused attention tends to give better throughput for long seq, but sometimes slightly worse TTFT on short sequences if it triggers extra workspace allocation. The matmul path can be faster for very short sequences. So it's a tradeoff.
02:08 Carlos: hm okay, and quantization — we currently run an 8-bit q8 profile in your config, is there a q4 option? We tried q4 in-house and saw quality drop.
02:19 Priya: yes we shipped q4 profiles, but quality varies by model and prompt. For your payment assistant we recommend q8 with selective higher-precision on attention/query compute for fidelity, that tends to preserve quality while giving some throughput gains. We can include A/B diff examples in the spreadsheet.
02:38 Jordan: quick recap of last week's benchmark: median TTFT 180ms, 95th 320ms under our synthetic load. Meridian's reported 95th 400ms under production mix. So gap is likely workload and cache coldness.
02:52 Ben: is there anything obvious in our setup? We're on dedicated pool with burst, pinned model, and KV cache enabled. We do see cache miss rate around 12% for new sessions.
03:07 Priya: 12% miss isn't huge but for checkout flows the first few tokens matter. If you can pre-warm the KV with a short prefix (like user context) before the UI asks the assistant to respond, TTFT improves. Also we saw some customers prefetch the first generated token by doing a lightweight low-temp call to initialize kernels.
03:30 Aisha: that prefetch idea might be complicated from a cost POV, but perhaps acceptable if it's low-cost. Also, any suggestions for streaming chunk sizes? We currently stream every 64 tokens.
03:41 Priya: streaming chunk size is another lever — smaller chunks lower per-chunk latency but increase scheduling overhead. For your mix we think 32-64 tokens is reasonable. However first-token latency is mostly separate — chunking only affects after the first token. If the first token is high, UI perceived latency is bad. Consider a hybrid: return first token as soon as available (non-blocking) and then stream in chunks.
04:06 Carlos: what's the effort to change kernel selection at runtime? We can't redeploy often.
04:12 Priya: you can set runtime policy per route in the console — pick kernel preference and fallback. We can prepare a one-line route override so you can test without infra changes. That should be low effort.
04:25 Jordan: also we can run a special bench where we mimic your session distribution — Priya, can you outline what we need from Meridian?
04:33 Priya: we need a sample of requests (anonymized) with sequence length histogram and a couple of representative prompts. Also traces showing TTFT per request and whether KV was warm. Carlos, Ben — can you share those by Friday?
04:44 Carlos: yes we'll dump anonymized histograms and sample traces, target EOD Fri (2026-11-13).
04:51 Ben: agreed. We'll include sample UI timing traces too.
04:56 Priya: excellent. Actionable tests we propose: 1) Kernel pinning experiment for short vs long sequences (A/B); 2) Streaming-first-token optimization (return first token asap then chunk); 3) 1-hour streaming run with production traffic and 2k sequence ceiling to measure tails.
05:18 Aisha: for the 1-hour run, we need to ensure monitoring hooks are in place — can Redwood push tracing tags or do we pull logs?
05:27 Priya: we push a small SDK snippet and tracer headers, but we can also configure our side to export server spans to your tracing endpoint. We'll include instructions.
05:38 Jordan: timeline — run the kernel A/B and streaming-first-token test early next week, then schedule the 1-hour streaming test mid-next week.
05:48 Carlos: sounds good. Any concerns about model fallback if a specialized kernel isn't available on some nodes?
05:55 Priya: we have fallback policies — if preferred kernel not available we fall back to compatible kernel, might increase latency. We'll surface that in the runbook and logs so you can correlate.
06:07 Ben: is there any SLA difference if we go Dedicated vs Private for these tests? We're on Dedicated currently.
06:14 Jordan: Dedicated gives predictable capacity; Private would give you more control over kernel images and KMS. For POC we think Dedicated is fine. If you need kernel-level control we'd recommend evaluating Private for longer term.
06:28 Carlos: noted. Also, security team asked about audit logs for inference requests — who has access to logs?
06:36 Priya: on Dedicated we preserve audit logs and redwood operators have access controlled via RBAC; for Private, logs remain in your VPC. We can include a SOC2 artifact and a pointer to our audit log retention doc.
06:50 Aisha: ok please share the security doc link.
06:54 Jordan: will do, Jordan to send SOC2 summary and audit log pointer after this call.
07:02 Priya: quick note on quantization — changing quantization requires a re-pack for the specific model variant and we can do that in a day for standard models, longer for custom fine-tuned ones.
07:15 Carlos: ours is a lightly fine-tuned open model, so okay.
07:19 Jordan: let's capture concrete commitments.
07:23 Priya: Action item: I'll share kernel config, one-line route override, and runbook for A/B testing by Thursday 2026-11-12.
07:33 Jordan: I'll share updated benchmark spreadsheet with median/95/99 columns and cost pro forma by Thursday 2026-11-12.
07:42 Carlos: we'll provide sequence length histograms and sample traces by Friday 2026-11-13 and confirm who will run the 1-hour streaming test on the 16th.
07:54 Ben: I'll coordinate with Aisha to run the 1-hour window.
08:00 Jordan: perfect. Any other questions?
08:04 Carlos: nothing else from me, thanks.
08:07 Aisha: no, thanks.
08:09 Jordan: thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts and book the tests.

Recap / Next Steps (verbatim from call):
- Priya: send kernel config + commands (due 2026-11-12)
- Jordan: updated benchmark spreadsheet and cost calc (due 2026-11-12)
